products.name: Nu Heru
products.subtitle: Chondrus crispus sea moss gel with baobab, elderberry and hibiscus. 300 ml or 500 ml.
products.standfirst: Chondrus crispus from the cold Atlantic, red before the baobab, elderberry and hibiscus go in. Named for Heru, the original Hero, out of the waters of Nu. 300 ml or 500 ml, glass jar.
body: Nu Heru starts from the same base as the rest of the sea moss shelf: Chondrus crispus, the red seaweed also called Irish moss or carrageen, which grows in cold Atlantic water rather than the warm farmed water some sea moss comes from. The name carries its own history, Heru, the original Hero, drawn out of the waters of Nu, the primordial waters life is said to have come from before there was land. To that base the jar adds baobab, elderberry and hibiscus, three plants with a long trade history of their own, the same dark red running through the whole gel.

No iodine figure is printed on this jar, the way there is on Seaking's capsule label, so no iodine claim sits on this page. Sea moss carries iodine and the amount moves with the harvest, which is exactly why a capsule, with a fixed dose, is the only format on this site allowed to print a number next to it.
Take it by the spoon: neat, stirred into a smoothie or juice, or into a warm tea with raw honey. Four named ingredients and the water the gel is prepared with, nothing else.

body: Mwani is Swahili for sea moss. Eucheuma cottonii is the species usually sold under that name, and it is a different plant to the cold-water Chondrus crispus the rest of this shelf runs on. It grows in warm, shallow Indian Ocean water, farmed on lines rather than picked off cold-water rock, which is part of why it costs less than the Atlantic jars, and part of why the colour runs deeper, to purple.

As with the other gels on this site, no iodine figure is printed for Purple Mwani, so no iodine claim is made about it here. If a measured number matters to you, Seaking prints 75 µg of iodine per capsule.
Use a clean spoon, take it neat or stirred into a smoothie. One tablespoon a day: about a 20 day jar. Two tablespoons a day: about ten.
